title: Projection maps of left adjoints are compatible with mates
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_1,\mathcal D_1,\mathcal C_2,\mathcal D_2$ be categories. For $i=1,2$ let $F_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$ be left adjoint to $G_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal C_i$, with unit $\eta_i$ and counit $\varepsilon_i$, and let $H_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal C_i$ be another functor. Let $T_i:\mathcal C_i\times\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_i$ and $S_i:\mathcal D_i\times\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal D_i$ be bifunctors. Give natural comparison maps
$$\delta_i(X,Y):T_i(G_iX,H_iY)\longrightarrow G_iS_i(X,Y)\qquad(X,Y\in\mathcal D_i).$$
For $K\in\mathcal C_i$, $M\in\mathcal D_i$, define $\pi_i(K,M):F_iT_i(K,H_iM)\to S_i(F_iK,M)$ as the adjoint transpose of
$$T_i(K,H_iM)\xrightarrow{T_i(\eta_{i,K},1)}T_i(G_iF_iK,H_iM)\xrightarrow{\delta_i(F_iK,M)}G_iS_i(F_iK,M).$$
Here adjoint transpose of $f:A\to G_iB$ means $\varepsilon_{i,B}\circ F_i(f)$; thus this definition fixes the projection map without any monoidal axioms.

Let $P:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ and $Q:\mathcal D_1\to\mathcal D_2$ be functors, with natural maps
$$p_{A,B}:P T_1(A,B)\to T_2(PA,PB),\qquad q_{X,Y}:Q S_1(X,Y)\to S_2(QX,QY).$$
Give natural transformations with components
$$\tau_X:P G_1X\to G_2QX,\quad\rho_Y:P H_1Y\to H_2QY,\quad b_K:F_2PK\to QF_1K.$$
Assume the following two equations (composition is right to left): for every $K\in\mathcal C_1$,
$$G_2(b_K)\circ\eta_{2,PK}=\tau_{F_1K}\circ P(\eta_{1,K});$$
and for every $X,Y\in\mathcal D_1$,
$$G_2(q_{X,Y})\circ\tau_{S_1(X,Y)}\circ P(\delta_1(X,Y))
=\delta_2(QX,QY)\circ T_2(1_{G_2QX},\rho_Y)\circ T_2(\tau_X,1_{PH_1Y})\circ p_{G_1X,H_1Y}.$$
Then for every $K\in\mathcal C_1$, $M\in\mathcal D_1$,
$$q_{F_1K,M}\circ Q(\pi_1(K,M))\circ b_{T_1(K,H_1M)}
=S_2(b_K,1_{QM})\circ\pi_2(PK,QM)\circ F_2(T_2(1_{PK},\rho_M))\circ F_2(p_{K,H_1M}).$$
This is an equality of maps $F_2P T_1(K,H_1M)\to S_2(QF_1K,QM)$, natural in $K,M$. None of the displayed comparison maps is required to be an isomorphism. All categorical data used here (bifunctors, natural transformations, adjunction units and counits, and their transposes) are explicitly specified in this statement. Categories have the identities and associative composition of [def-nagata-category]. A functor preserves identities and composition; a bifunctor is a functor from a product category. A natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ has components $\alpha_X:FX\to GX$ satisfying $G(f)\circ\alpha_X=\alpha_Y\circ F(f)$ for every $f:X\to Y$. The units and counits satisfy the two adjunction triangle identities. The mate and adjoint-transpose conventions are those of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

lean.statement:
lemma projectionMap_mate
    (hβ : ∀ K, adj₂.unit.app (U.obj K) ≫ G₂.map (β.app K) =
      U.map (adj₁.unit.app K) ≫ τ.app (F₁.obj K))
    (hδ : ∀ X Y, U.map ((δ₁.app X).app Y) ≫ τ.app ((T'₁.obj X).obj Y) ≫
        G₂.map ((ψV.app X).app Y) =
      (ψU.app (G₁.obj X)).app (G'₁.obj Y) ≫ (T₂.map (τ.app X)).app _ ≫
        (T₂.obj _).map (τ'.app Y) ≫ (δ₂.app (V.obj X)).app (V.obj Y))
    (K : C₁) (M : D₁) :
    β.app ((T₁.obj K).obj (G'₁.obj M)) ≫
        V.map (((adj₁.projectionMap G'₁ T₁ T'₁ δ₁).app K).app M) ≫
        (ψV.app (F₁.obj K)).app M =
      F₂.map ((ψU.app K).app (G'₁.obj M)) ≫ F₂.map ((T₂.obj (U.obj K)).map (τ'.app M)) ≫
        ((adj₂.projectionMap G'₂ T₂ T'₂ δ₂).app (U.obj K)).app (V.obj M) ≫
        (T'₂.map (β.app K)).app (V.obj M)
